objective: Transform labeled synthetic CASREP messages through validated authoring, immutable review, return/revision, conflict resolution and local mock release with traceable exports.

invocation.input: Object with action string. action=parse requires message:string. action=workflow requires reportId:string, revisions:array of revision snapshots and commands:array of command objects defined in rules. action=reconcile requires base,left,right objects of fifteen string content fields. No optional fields, defaults or null inputs except ignored extra properties; empty revisions/commands permitted.
invocation.output: Exactly the action-specific JSON object defined in rules; invalid envelope/shape returns exactly {error:string}. parse validation failures use its normal envelope. workflow command failures use its normal last-accepted-state envelope. reconcile merged has all fifteen content strings; conflicts array canonical field order.
rules: All actions are deterministic synthetic calculations, never model calls or official transmission. POST /api/invoke receives the raw object. No action may trust expected, state or approval flags from fixture data. Extra object properties are ignored. Missing required properties, wrong types or null return {"error":"input: invalid shape"}; unknown action returns {"error":"action: unsupported"}. Shape checks precede domain checks. No throws for domain failures.

Nested workflow shape checks require reportId matching SYN-CR-NNN, revisions and commands arrays; every revision has the eight documented properties of their documented types, content has the fifteen required string fields, parentRevisionIds an array of strings; all six command fields are strings, timestamp a real UTC timestamp. Duplicate revision IDs or parent/content/source inconsistencies are domain lineage errors on save. For reconcile, each of base/left/right must have all fifteen string fields. For parse, message must be string (empty string is permitted and yields grammar error). Any nested shape failure returns only {"error":"input: invalid shape"}.

parse uses exactly the fictional grammar documented in data/README.md: UTF-8, fifteen ordered KEY=value lines then END and terminal LF. Split first equals; preserve values literally. Output exactly {parsedFields,validationErrors,renderedMessage}. parsedFields contains all fifteen string fields in canonical order (missing values empty). renderedMessage is canonical text on success and null on any error. validationErrors is an ordered string array.

Grammar errors precede value errors and produce only ["message: expected canonical KEY=value lines and END"]. A missing known key is treated as an empty field, not grammar failure; all other remaining keys must retain order. Unknown/duplicate/out-of-order keys, CR, missing END or terminal LF are grammar failures. Empty or missing value yields "<field>: required" except marking uses "marking: synthetic marking required". Value errors accumulate in canonical field order, one error per field.

MARKING must equal "Synthetic — not validated against the real CASREP format.". REPORT matches ^SYN-CR-[0-9]{3}$, FAMILY matches ^SYN-FAM-[0-9]{3}$; errors "reportId: expected SYN-CR-NNN" and "familyId: expected SYN-FAM-NNN". TYPE enum INITIAL, UPDATE, CORRECT, CASCOR, otherwise "reportType: expected INITIAL, UPDATE, CORRECT or CASCOR". CATEGORY string 2/3/4 else "category: expected 2, 3 or 4".

INITIAL RELATED=NONE; other types RELATED matches report ID grammar and differs from REPORT; error "relatedReportId: invalid link". Parse checks no runtime predecessor. All other text fields nonempty and preserved without trimming. OCCURRED real calendar UTC timestamp exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ; error "occurredAt: expected a real UTC timestamp YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ". REPAIR same format and >= OCCURRED, otherwise "repair: expected UTC timestamp at or after occurredAt"; CASCOR instead requires COMPLETE or "repair: CASCOR requires COMPLETE". STATUS DEGRADED/UNAVAILABLE, or CASCOR RESTORED; errors "equipmentStatus: expected DEGRADED or UNAVAILABLE" and "equipmentStatus: CASCOR requires RESTORED".

workflow starts EMPTY with currentRevisionId NONE, holder Originator (Sailor/LPO), no audit or approvals. revisions supplies immutable snapshots, not initial state. Replay commands in input order; save introduces referenced revision. Command fields: eventId, actorId, timestamp, revisionId, action, text (all strings); text may be empty except return/comment. Timestamp must be real UTC. eventId unique. Supported commands save, submit, comment, return, approveForward, approve, mockRelease. Unsupported command yields "action: unsupported". Stop at first rejected command and return last accepted state plus one rejection. Never accept caller role, status or approval flags.

workflow output exactly {status,holder,currentRevisionId,revisionIds,auditEventIds,validApprovalEventIds,invalidatedApprovalEventIds,renderedMessage,errors,rejections}. status EMPTY/DRAFT/IN_REVIEW/RETURNED/APPROVED/RELEASED; holder uses six named roles or NONE; revisionIds are successfully saved revision IDs in save order; audit IDs and approvals in command order; invalidated IDs in original approval order. renderedMessage null before save, otherwise current canonical message. errors empty or [first rejection reason]; rejections empty or [{actorId,action,revisionId,reason}].

Actors ACT-01 through ACT-06 map in order to Originator (Sailor/LPO), Division Officer, Department Head, Engineer Officer/CHENG, XO, CO; any other actor rejected "actorId: role is not permitted". Role simulation is not authentication. Only originator saves/submits. Other misuse is "actorId: role is not permitted". For decision actions, current holder must act; error "currentHolder: <holder> must act next".

Precedence after shape/command validation: unauthorized actor; duplicate eventId ("eventId: duplicate"); released (mockRelease: "status: report already released", all others "status: released report is immutable; create a linked report"); non-save revision mismatch ("revisionId: current revision is <id>"); originator return ("action: originator cannot return its own draft"); CO approveForward ("action: CO has no next reviewer"); action-specific guards below. Failed command appends no successful audit and changes no accepted state.

save validates referenced revision sourceMessage and content equality; errors from parse first, else "revision: invalid lineage" for absent snapshot, mismatched report/content/source, duplicate ID, or parents not exactly current ID (first save parents empty). Revisions use revisionId,reportId,parentRevisionIds,content,sourceMessage,actorId,timestamp,changeReason as in data/README.md. A save resets DRAFT and originator holder; invalidates every prior valid approval. comment from any of six roles preserves status, content and holder; requires text.trim nonempty else "text: required". return requires IN_REVIEW and holder downstream, nonblank reason, resets RETURNED and originator holder and invalidates all approvals.

submit requires DRAFT or RETURNED else "status: submission requires DRAFT or RETURNED"; sends to Division Officer, IN_REVIEW. approveForward requires IN_REVIEW and current holder Division Officer through XO, appends approval and advances one role. approve requires CO holder and IN_REVIEW, appends approval, sets APPROVED with CO holder. Invalid status for these decisions returns "status: review requires IN_REVIEW". return has same status error. approve by non-CO returns "actorId: role is not permitted".

mockRelease requires CO. If DRAFT/RETURNED or approvals were invalidated, error "approvals: current revision requires all five reviewer approvals"; otherwise without current CO approval error "approvals: CO approval required for current revision". All five approvals must match current revision. Success RELEASED/NONE, frozen content. It is separate from approve and does not add an approval. No automatic transitions.

reconcile accepts base,left,right content objects with all fifteen string fields. Output exactly {conflicts,merged}. Iterate canonical content field order. When left==right use it; when left==base use right; when right==base use left; otherwise append {field,base,left,right} and retain base value in merged. No clock-based winner. This field comparison is used above the foundation DAG validation in the actual app. Empty conflicts does not mean approved.

UI durable commands use the same workflow logic before atomic commit. File state is outside runtime allowlist in a local data directory; acknowledge Saved only after fsync/rename. Serialize commits and reject stale base revision, preserving draft. Failed saves/exports never append successful events or partial downloads. Rejections persist separately with monotonic attemptId, actorId,action,revisionId,reason and server UTC timestamp. No credentials. Client dirty buffer persists locally and requires save/discard before approving committed content.

UI supports linked INITIAL→UPDATE→CORRECT→CASCOR using predecessor released, same family/equipment/JSN and new IDs, no inherited approval. CASCOR closes family only after its mock release. Explicit supersession/cancellation/expiry are local lifecycle notices retaining released snapshots and audit; no operational deadlines invented. Foundation core invocation remains pure; browser persistence and these lifecycle operations are tested as integration requirements, not accepted from precomputed states.

A valid workflow envelope with empty commands returns EMPTY, originator holder, currentRevisionId NONE, empty revisionIds/auditEventIds/approval arrays/errors/rejections, renderedMessage null. Only saved revisions appear in revisionIds. Workflow validation errors on save are the first parse validation error in canonical order. A missing referenced save snapshot yields "revision: invalid lineage". An unsupported command action returns workflow errors ["action: unsupported"] and one rejection, preserving accepted prefix. Nonempty trimmed decision text is required for comment/return; other action texts may be empty. Extra fields are ignored even on content objects; required fifteen content fields define comparison and rendering.

capabilities.description: Parse and render all four synthetic CASREP types, validate canonical fields and preserve inert narrative.
Replay explicit actor decisions, enforce six roles, current revision, return loop and five fresh approvals before local mock release.
Retain immutable branches, expose differing fields and require a resolution referencing both heads.
